column1: # Manufacturer specifications, transcribed to check the reference set against
# Sources: flyozone.com and the manufacturers' own published tables
# A dash means the maker does not publish that figure.
# BGD's rows were completed on 2026-10-06 from flybgd.com (the Lynx 2 page,
# its "Specifications" table; flybubble.com carries the same table). BGD
# publish a centre chord, a "Total line length", a line "Height" and — alone
# among the makers here — a "Linear scaling factor" for each size. Ozone
# publish none of the last three.
# This note used to say BGD do not publish a root chord, and that the five in
# `size-families.tsv` were "an estimate already in the reference data". They
# are BGD's published centre chord. What was true is what happened first: I
# filled these five in from area and span, the check reported five
# disagreements, and I took that for a published figure disagreeing with an
# estimate when it was my arithmetic disagreeing with a published figure. A
# cross-check that compares a guess with anything reads like evidence.
# total_line_m here is what BGD publish. It is NOT the length of their
# lineset — see the head of `size-families.tsv` — and it is kept for that
# reason: the sum of the maker's own line sheets is the measurement, and this
# is the figure that disagrees with it.
# `size-families.tsv` is what this project measures against. Nothing checked
# that IT was right. These are the manufacturers' own figures, kept separate
# so the two can disagree: a single file cannot check itself.

# 22.1 m2 and AR 5.15 where the website says 22.2 and 5.16) the website table
